criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: First two lines name the claim verbatim, anchor it to federal dollars being scoped now, and signal a correction without snark; the 210-char cutoff lands cleanly mid-premise-challenge.

criteria.name: Claim load-bearing + AK stakes
criteria.notes: NORAD/USNORTHCOM 2026-2030 modernization and Alaska-based contractor competition named explicitly; one point off because the DAF solicitation is flagged as 'potential' and no dollar figure is cited.

criteria.name: Steelman fairness
criteria.notes: Paragraph 3 is generous, accurate, and unsnarky: credits the GEO physical limitation, validates sensor fusion as genuinely unsolved, and would leave a Boufard reader feeling fairly represented.

criteria.name: Counter-evidence quality
criteria.notes: Iridium NEXT rebuttal rests on ESA eoPortal primary source with orbital specifics; Starlink rebuttal rests on a single credible secondary (High North News), not a primary or two independent outlets, which keeps this below 10.

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Named specifics appear every one to two sentences throughout: 66 satellites, 86.4-degree inclination, six planes, Sea Area A4, 2022, 2026-2030, NORAD, USNORTHCOM, MeriTalk, January 2026, UAF, West Point.

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: Boufard attribution traces to confirmed live MeriTalk primary; Iridium NEXT traces to ESA eoPortal primary; Starlink traces to High North News, a single credible secondary outlet only, not a primary or two independent sources.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, structural, position-taking, no banned phrases, no influencer cadence, corrective without contempt; reads precisely like the brand voice descriptor.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: All paragraphs are two to four sentences, body word count approximately 392 (within 350-475), total character count well under 3000, easy to scan on desktop and mobile.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Closing question is real, debatable, industry-specific, and tied directly to the corrected frame (LEO vs GEO trade study); not generic and not a CTA.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: A program manager can immediately name the decision to reframe: treat LEO polar coverage as available infrastructure in the trade study rather than writing it off with GEO-belt assumptions.

hard_fail_checks.name: hashtag_count_in_range
hard_fail_checks.notes: 4 hashtags, all drawn from brand.yaml whitelist (AlaskaAI, DefenseTech, ArcticInnovation, FederalContracting), placed at end only.

hard_fail_checks.name: punctuation_bans_held
hard_fail_checks.notes: No em-dashes, en-dashes, double-hyphens, colons, or semicolons found anywhere in the post body.

hard_fail_checks.name: total_char_count_under_linkedin_cap
hard_fail_checks.notes: Total post character count is approximately 2617, well under the 3000-character LinkedIn cap.

hard_fail_checks.name: word_count_in_range
hard_fail_checks.notes: Body word count is approximately 392 words (hashtag line excluded), within the 350-475 range.

hard_fail_checks.name: claim_is_attributed
hard_fail_checks.notes: Troy Boufard is named with title and institutional affiliation; the verbatim quote is present and matches claim_dossier.json selected_claim.claim_verbatim; MeriTalk January 2026 is cited inline.

hard_fail_checks.name: steelman_present
hard_fail_checks.notes: Paragraph 3 states the strongest honest version of the claim before any rebuttal, consistent with claim_dossier.json selected_claim.steelman, and covers both the GEO physical limitation and the sensor fusion bottleneck.

one_sentence_fix: Corroborate the Starlink polar coverage claim with a second independent source (such as SpaceX regulatory filings or an FCC authorization document) so every rebuttal point meets the two-independent-credible-outlets standard.
